title: Seaford Creek and Unqua Neck Cultural Landscape
summary: A south shore estuarine landscape tied to Native village life, shellfishing, fishing, bay travel, and coastal resource use in Merrick and Massapequa homelands.
address_label: Seaford Creek / Unqua Neck waterways, Seaford-Massapequa area
ancestral_territory_note: Within the wider Merrick/Massapequa south shore cultural landscape; linked here to Merrick Ancestral Land with care about overlapping homelands.
why_this_matters: Seaford Creek and Unqua Neck show why tidal waterways and neck lands mattered: they were living landscapes, travel routes, and foodways rather than empty marshes.
introduction_content:
An Illustrated History of Massapequa identifies Seaford Creek and Unqua Neck among the coastal places associated with Native habitation and estuarine resource use. These waterways offered access to shellfish, fish, wetlands, and bay travel.

The broader creek-and-neck landscape shows why tidal waterways mattered, while avoiding directions to shoreline lots or cultural deposits.
